172	  h=$(hostname -f 2>/dev/null || hostname 2>/dev/null)
173	  ip=$(hostname -I 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
174	fi
175	[ -z "$ip" ] && ip="?"
176	[ -z "$h" ] && h="?"
177	printf 'MOD_network=%s|%s\n' "$h" "$ip"
178	
179	# --- fastfetch (optional, behind sentinel) ---
180	if [ "${FLEET_FF:-0}" = "1" ]; then
181	  if command -v fastfetch >/dev/null 2>&1; then
182	    printf 'FF_BEGIN\n'
183	    fastfetch --format json 2>/dev/null
184	    printf '\nFF_END\n'
185	  else
186	    printf 'FF_BEGIN\nERR:not-installed\nFF_END\n'
187	  fi
188	fi
189	"""
190	
191	
192	@dataclass
193	class HostInfo:
194	    host: str
195	    status: str  # "ok" | "N/A"
196	    modules: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
197	    fastfetch: dict | str | None = None
198	    error: str | None = None
199	    elapsed_ms: int = 0
200	
201	
202	def _parse_value(mod: str, raw: str) -> Any:
203	    """Translate MOD_<name>=<raw> into a structured value.
204	
205	    Returns either a dict, the raw string, or {"_err": msg} for ERR:<msg>.
206	    """
207	    if raw.startswith("ERR:"):
208	        return {"_err": raw[4:]}
209	    if mod == "cpu":
210	        parts = raw.split("|", 1)
211	        return {"model": parts[0], "cores": int(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 and parts[1].isdigit() else None}
212	    if mod in {"mem", "disk"}:
213	        parts = raw.split("|")
214	        if len(parts) != 2 or not all(p.isdigit() for p in parts):
215	            return {"_err": "parse"}
216	        used, total = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1])
217	        return {"used_bytes": used, "total_bytes": total, "used_pct": (used / total * 100) if total else 0}
218	    if mod == "load":
219	        parts = raw.split("|")
220	        if len(parts) != 3:
221	            return {"_err": "parse"}
222	        try:
223	            return {"l1": float(parts[0]), "l5": float(parts[1]), "l15": float(parts[2])}
224	        except ValueError:
225	            return {"_err": "parse"}
226	    if mod == "uptime":
227	        try:
228	            return {"seconds": int(raw)}
229	        except ValueError:
230	            return {"_err": "parse"}
231	    if mod == "docker":
232	        parts = raw.split("|")
233	        if len(parts) != 2:
234	            return {"_err": "parse"}
235	        try:
236	            return {"running": int(parts[0]), "total": int(parts[1])}
237	        except ValueError:
238	            return {"_err": "parse"}
239	    if mod == "chezmoi":
240	        parts = raw.split("|")
241	        return {"status_lines": parts[0], "commits_behind": parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else "?"}
242	    if mod == "gpu":
243	        parts = raw.split("|")
244	        if len(parts) == 3:  # nvidia-smi: name|used_mb|total_mb
245	            try:
246	                return {"name": parts[0], "vram_used_mb": int(parts[1]), "vram_total_mb": int(parts[2])}
247	            except ValueError:
248	                return {"name": raw, "vram_used_mb": None, "vram_total_mb": None}
249	        return {"name": raw, "vram_used_mb": None, "vram_total_mb": None}

122

135	        ps_type = (ps.get("type") or "none").lower()
136	        if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):

143	        host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
144	        host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}

1	# Custom SSH config channel for television (tv)
2	# Parses Host entries from ~/.ssh/config AND ~/.ssh/config.d/* (Include support).
3	# The community ssh-hosts channel only reads ~/.ssh/config directly.
4	#
5	# Each entry shows which file the host is defined in, so duplicates across
6	# config.d/* are easy to spot. The output (what gets passed to ssh / actions)
7	# is just the bare hostname.
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   tv ssh-config
11	#
12	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
13	#   Enter      SSH into selected host
14	#   Alt+T      Online probe: BatchMode=yes test (does pubkey login actually work?)
15	#   Alt+A      Offline batch scan: list every host + whether a local key file exists
16	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel

19	# (no network — just stat the IdentityFile paths).

28	# actions still receive a clean hostname via {split:\t:1}.
29	command = """
30	for f in $HOME/.ssh/config $HOME/.ssh/config.d/*; do
31	  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
32	  rel=${f#$HOME/}
33	  awk -v src="$rel" '
34	    /^[[:space:]]*Host[[:space:]]/ {
35	      for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {
36	        if ($i !~ /[*?]/) printf "%s\\t%s\\n", src, $i
37	      }
38	    }' "$f"

40	"""
41	display = "{split:\\t:1}  ({split:\\t:0})"
42	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
43	
44	[preview]

46	host='{split:\\t:1}'
47	src='{split:\\t:0}'
48	echo "# defined in: $src"
49	echo
50	ssh -G "$host" 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^(host|hostname|user|port|identityfile|proxycommand|proxyjump|forwardagent|identityagent|localforward|remoteforward)[[:space:]]'
51	echo
52	echo '--- local key check (offline) ---'
53	found=0
54	while IFS= read -r f; do

57	  if [ -f "$f" ]; then

59	    found=1
60	  else

62	  fi

65	EOF
66	if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then

69	  echo '     (or relies on ssh-agent / IdentityAgent — try Alt+T to probe)'
70	fi

100	  *)   echo "[FAIL] remote command failed (exit $rc) — auth probably OK but 'true' failed" ;;

24	The `fleet chezmoi <action>` namespace was introduced to free the top

26	LONGER top-level subcommands — they only exist under `chezmoi`. The
27	`just fleet-*` recipes still call scripts/fleet/apply.py directly with
28	its underlying flags (`--readiness`, `--status`, `--kill-orphans`,
29	`--compact`, etc.) and continue to work unchanged.

32	back to ~/.local/share/chezmoi), so the binary works from any cwd.

49	                          Run chezmoi update --init across the fleet.

51	  chezmoi status --quick  Skip remote `git fetch` (faster).
52	  chezmoi status --live   Process-liveness probe (use during/after apply).
53	  chezmoi status --live --watch N  Poll every N seconds.

75	                          Cross-host argv-list command runner. Argv after

78	                          rc-loaded env; --ai for succeeded/differed/failed

85	  fleet tmux --hosts self,ts_nas     # tmux sessions, 2 hosts

125	    """Forward to scripts.fleet.apply.main() with argv swap."""
126	    sys.argv = ["fleet apply", *forwarded]

134	       --quick        → --readiness --readiness-no-fetch
135	       --live         → --status
136	       --live --watch → --status --watch N (default 10)
137	    """
138	    live = "--live" in args
139	    quick = "--quick" in args
140	    rest = [a for a in args if a not in ("--live", "--quick")]
141	    if live:

143	        # Default watch interval when --live is passed without a numeric --watch
144	        if "--watch" not in rest:

148	        if quick:

558	def _connect_kwargs(host: Host) -> dict:
559	    """Translate Host -> asyncssh.connect kwargs.
560	
561	    asyncssh reads ~/.ssh/config by default for the `host` arg. When ssh_alias
562	    is set we pass it as `host` and let asyncssh resolve hostname/user/port/
563	    IdentityFile/ProxyJump from ssh_config. Explicit fields override.
564	    """
565	    target = host.ssh_alias or host.hostname
566	    assert target is not None  # validated in load_hosts
567	    kwargs: dict = {"host": target, "known_hosts": None}
568	    # known_hosts=None tells asyncssh to skip its own check; we still rely on
569	    # the user having ssh'd manually first (StrictHostKeyChecking is enforced
570	    # implicitly by them adding it to ~/.ssh/known_hosts ahead of time).
571	    # Switching to known_hosts=() would force strict but reject every new host.
572	    if host.user:
573	        kwargs["username"] = host.user
574	    if host.port:
575	        kwargs["port"] = host.port
576	    if host.identity_file:
577	        kwargs["client_keys"] = [str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
578	    return kwargs

453	# Fleet (multi-host chezmoi apply)
454	# ============================================================================
455	# Run `chezmoi update --init` (or apply / diff) across many remote hosts in
456	# parallel. Inventory: ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml (seeded by chezmoi as a
457	# `create_private_` template — your edits are preserved). Sudo password
458	# sources: plain / interactive prompt / Bitwarden CLI / none.
459	# Per-host log: logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log
460	# Exit code = number of failed hosts.

462	
463	# Umbrella `fleet` CLI — same binary chezmoi deploys to ~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet,
464	# but run from the source tree (works before first `chezmoi apply`). Subcommands:
465	# apply / status / diff / tail / kill / compact / edit / tmux / info / pueue.
466	# Prefer this over `fleet-*` recipes when invoking from inside the repo;
467	# the old recipes stay as muscle-memory aliases.
468	fleet *ARGS:
469	    @uv run --script ./dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet {{ARGS}}
470	
471	# MLflow CLI umbrella — wraps `tv mlflow` plus open / copy / plot / list /
472	# download subcommands. See dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf for surface.
473	mlf *ARGS:
474	    @uv run --script ./dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf {{ARGS}}
475	
476	# Apply chezmoi update to all configured hosts in parallel
477	fleet-apply *ARGS:
478	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py {{ARGS}}
479	
480	# Edit fleet inventory (~/.config/fleet/machines.toml). Seeds an empty
481	# template on first run; opens with $EDITOR (defaults to nvim).
482	fleet-edit:
483	    @mkdir -p ~/.config/fleet
484	    @if [ ! -f ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml ]; then \
485	        echo "[INFO] seeding empty ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — add [[hosts]] entries below"; \
486	        printf '# fleet-apply inventory — see docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md\n# Schema reference: dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl\n\n[defaults]\nchezmoi_path    = "auto"\nconnect_timeout = 30\ncommand_timeout = 7200\n\n# [[hosts]]\n# name      = "lab-box"\n# ssh_alias = "lab-box"\n# no_root_machine = false\n# password_source = { type = "prompt" }\n' > ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml; \
487	        chmod 600 ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml; \
488	    fi
489	    "${EDITOR:-nvim}" ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
490	
491	
492	# Pre-flight readiness probe across all configured hosts. Predicts what
493	# `just fleet-apply` would do per host (up-to-date / behind / drift / busy
494	# / toml-mismatch / not-init / unreachable / ...) WITHOUT changing anything.
495	# Read-only, ~1.5s per host (with `git fetch`). See docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md
496	# § Readiness probe.
497	fleet-status *ARGS:
498	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --readiness {{ARGS}}
499	
500	# Like fleet-status but skip remote `git fetch` (faster, but 'behind' state
501	# may be stale). Useful offline or when you only care about drift / busy.
502	fleet-status-quick *ARGS:
503	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --readiness --readiness-no-fetch {{ARGS}}
504	
505	
506	# Preview only: runs `chezmoi diff` on every host (no changes applied)
507	fleet-apply-dry-run *ARGS:
508	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --dry-run {{ARGS}}
509	
510	# Quick `chezmoi diff` against ONE host (serial, debug-friendly output).
511	# Use this in vibe loops to see exactly what your latest commit will do
512	# on a specific machine before pushing/applying for real.
513	fleet-diff HOST *ARGS:
514	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --dry-run --hosts {{HOST}} --serial {{ARGS}}
515	
516	# Apply ONLY a single chezmoi target on each host (skips ansible / Brewfile).
517	# PATH is the chezmoi target path, e.g. `.config/zsh/aliases.zsh` or
518	# `.zshrc`. Fast feedback for editing one dotfile across the fleet without
519	# waiting for full Linuxbrew/ansible cycles. Pass extra `--hosts HOST` to
520	# scope. Internally sets CHEZMOI_FLEET_APPLY_PATH so the wrapper runs
521	# `chezmoi apply <relpath>` instead of `chezmoi update --init`.
522	fleet-apply-file PATH *ARGS:

528	# on divergence — use `just fleet-apply-branch-force` to nuke local
529	# state with `git reset --hard`. Local hosts skip this entirely (source

531	fleet-apply-branch BRANCH *ARGS:

547	
548	# Probe each host for running chezmoi/ansible (use after killing local SSH)

551	
552	# Like fleet-apply-status but re-poll every Ns until everyone is idle
553	# (Ctrl+C to stop). Default interval 10s; override with --watch=N in ARGS.
554	fleet-apply-watch *ARGS:
555	    ./scripts/fleet/apply.py --status --watch 10 {{ARGS}}
556	
557	# Live-tail the remote fleet-apply log of HOST (defaults to most recent run);
558	# pass `HOST:RUN_ID` (e.g. lab-box:20260422T133615Z) to pin a specific run.
559	# Ctrl+C stops the viewer only — the remote run keeps going.

562

```text
1	# tv vs fzf — Comparison & Best Practices
2	
3	Two fuzzy finders, two philosophies. This dotfiles repo uses **both**.
4	
5	| | **fzf** | **television (tv)** |
6	|---|---------|---------------------|
7	| Philosophy | Low-level fuzzy primitive; you compose workflows with shell glue | Structured picker framework; workflows declared as TOML channels |
8	| Analogy | Unix pipe building block | Terminal-native Telescope.nvim |
9	| Matcher | Custom mature engine (multi-year, battle-tested) | [nucleo](https://github.com/helix-editor/nucleo) (shared with Helix) |
10	| Query syntax | fuzzy, exact (`'`), prefix (`^`), suffix (`$`), inverse (`!`), **OR** (`\|`) | fuzzy, exact, prefix, suffix, substring, negate — no OR |
11	| Extensibility | Shell scripts, env vars, `--bind`, `--preview`, `--reload` | TOML channel files in `cable/` directory |
12	| Shell integration | `Ctrl+R` / `Ctrl+T` / `Alt+C` + `**<TAB>` completion | `Ctrl+R` / `Ctrl+T` with context-aware channel triggers |
13	| Sorting control | `--tiebreak`, `--sort`, `--no-sort` | `no_sort`, `frecency` per channel |
14	| Multi-select | `--multi` + Tab/Shift-Tab | Built-in |
15	| Preview | `--preview` flag (any command) | `[preview]` section in channel TOML |
16	| Actions on select | `--bind 'enter:execute(...)'` | `[actions]` section; fork/execute modes |
17	| Ecosystem maturity | Huge: vim, tmux, zsh, bash, fish, git, kubectl, etc. | Growing; fewer third-party integrations |
18	| Config in this repo | `dot_config/zsh/tools/10_fzf.zsh` | `dot_config/television/cable/*.toml` |
19	
20	## When to use which (in this dotfiles repo)
21	
22	| Use case | Tool | Why |
23	|----------|------|-----|
24	| Shell history (`Ctrl+R`) | fzf | More sorting modes, `FZF_CTRL_R_OPTS` customization |
25	| File picker (`Ctrl+T`) | fzf | Deep completion integration, `**<TAB>` |
26	| Directory cd (`Alt+C`) | fzf | Built-in, simple |
27	| Tab completion preview | fzf | `_fzf_comprun` per-command previews |
28	| Sesh session picker | tv | Channel with source cycling (tmux/zoxide/config/fd), preview, kill action |
29	| CLI tools picker | tv | Channel parsing `cli-tools.md`, preview with tldr |
30	| Aliases picker | tv | Channel listing all runtime aliases/functions |
31	| Git branch switching | tv | Channel with preview + checkout action |
32	| Custom domain pickers | tv | Declarative TOML channels are faster to author than shell wrappers |
33	
34	## "Telescope-like workflow" explained
35	
36	The pattern (popularized by [telescope.nvim](https://github.com/nvim-telescope/telescope.nvim)):
37	
38	```
39	Source → Filter/Sort → Preview → Action
40	```
41	
42	You use the **same picker UI** with **different data sources**. Each picker (channel) defines what to search, how to preview, and what actions are available. You don't switch mental models — just switch channels.
43	
44	tv implements this natively: each `.toml` file in `cable/` is a channel recipe.
45	
46	## Channel / Cable Best Practices
47	
48	### 1. One channel = one job
49	
50	Don't build a mega-channel. Keep each channel focused:

All top-level subcommands forward to `scripts/fleet/{module}.py` by dynamic import and argv swap (lines 126–128).

### 2. **Fleet Inventory Schema**

**Location:** `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` (user-editable after first chezmoi apply)  
**Template:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/fleet/create_private_machines.toml.tmpl`

**Host fields (from `Host` dataclass, apply.py lines 65–90):**
- `name` (string, required, unique)
- `ssh_alias` (preferred) OR `hostname` + `user` + `port` + `identity_file` (explicit connection)
- `local` (bool; True = run locally, no SSH)
- `no_root_machine` (bool; matches `.chezmoi.toml` noRoot setting)
- `chezmoi_path` (default: "auto"; can override per-host)
- `password_source` (dict: `{type: "plain"|"prompt"|"bitwarden"|"none", value/item: ...}`)
- `extra_env` (dict of env vars to inject)

**Representative entry (template lines 49–52):**
```toml
[[hosts]]
name            = "lab-box"
ssh_alias       = "lab-box"
no_root_machine = false
password_source = { type = "bitwarden", item = "ssh-lab-box-sudo" }
```

---

### 3. **Python Subcommand Modules Summary**

**Shared inventory loader:** `__init__.py` (lines 19–28) re-exports from `apply.py`:
- `load_hosts(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Host], dict]` (apply.py:103)
- `_connect_kwargs(host: Host) -> dict` (apply.py:558)
- `Host` dataclass, constants (`DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH`, etc.)

**Per-module (by size):**

1. **tmux.py (429 lines)** — Cross-host tmux session summary. Fans out `tmux list-sessions` via remote dispatcher, prefers deployed `.config/tmux/tmux-session-summary.py --json` on remote, fallback to raw `tmux` commands. Output: Rich table (default) or JSON. All six subcommands use identical pattern: `load_hosts()` → `_filter_hosts()` → asyncio gather over parallelized `_run_one(host)` → render.

2. **pueue.py (443 lines)** — Cross-host pueue queue summary. Runs `pueue status --json` remotely, pipes through local `pqsum json --raw-stdin --host=NAME` for filtering, `--ai` mode aggregates to `pqsum ai --stdin-json --multi-host` for LLM summary. Same orchestration pattern.

3. **info.py (529 lines)** — Cross-host system snapshot (OS/CPU/memory/disk/load/uptime/docker/chezmoi modules). Embeds one large bash blob (`_BASH_PROBE`, ~188 lines) that emits `MOD_<name>=<value>` lines per module (or `ERR:<msg>` on failure). No per-host failures abort the fleet. `--full` adds GPU/network; `--ff` runs `fastfetch --format json` instead.

4. **exec.py (833 lines)** — Cross-host argv-list command runner. Default: safe argv list (no shell expansion). `--shell bash` opt-in for pipes/globs; `--login` loads rc files (nvm/mise/conda); `--ai` classifies per-host output into succeeded/differed/failed tiers (copy-pasted AICAP block, extraction TODO). Output: table, JSON, `--out-dir`, or `--full-output` blocks.

5. **apply.py (3100 lines)** — Chezmoi deployment orchestrator (not primarily a "subcommand" but the backend for `fleet chezmoi *`). Only reference to it as a standalone module is `_dispatch_apply()` forwarding.

**Smallest/best template:** `tmux.py` is the most minimal picker-friendly module: it has no complex filtering, no subprocess delegation, and a clean `HostResult` struct + table renderer.

**Single `--host NAME` argument pattern:** None of the subcommands currently accept a single `--host NAME` flag to isolate one host (they all use `--hosts COMMA_LIST`). However, `exec.py` has `--out-dir DIR` for per-host file output, suggesting a template for single-host pipelines could be modeled there.

---

### 4. **Television Cable Installation & SSH Config**

**Location:** `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml`

**Deployment:** `dot_config/television/cable/` → `~/.config/television/cable/` (chezmoi deploys via `dot_` prefix)

**Status:** `ssh-config.toml` is a fully functional `tv` cable picker with:
- **Source:** reads `~/.ssh/config` + `~/.ssh/config.d/*` (with Include support)
- **Display:** shows host origin file in preview
- **Actions:** Enter to SSH, Alt+T to probe, Alt+A for offline key scan
- **Preview:** resolves `ssh -G`, shows local key files

**For fleet hosts:** Dropping a new `fleet-hosts.toml` cable file here would be viable *if* you want TV as the primary UX. However, since fleet has its own `machines.toml` inventory (independent of `~/.ssh/config`), **a Python `fleet hosts` picker subcommand is more direct** — it avoids duplication and keeps fleet self-contained. TV cable is better suited for `ssh-config` (which chezmoi/ansible/direct SSH already consume), not fleet-specific logic.

---

### 5. **Existing Host-Listing Flag**

No dedicated `--list-hosts` or host enumeration flag exists in any subcommand. All support `--hosts COMMA_LIST` (inclusion) and `--exclude COMMA_LIST` (exclusion), but there's no "enumerate all available hosts" output mode. You'd need to add one if the picker is to prompt interactively, or just directly read `machines.toml` via `load_hosts()` in your new subcommand.

## Fleet Surface Map

### 1. **Justfile `fleet*` Recipes**

| Recipe | One-line description | Underlying script |
|--------|---------------------|------------------|
| `fleet` | Umbrella CLI (apply/status/diff/tail/kill/compact/edit/tmux/info/pueue) | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` |
| `mlf` | MLflow CLI umbrella (tv mlflow + open/copy/plot/list/download) | `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf` |
| `fleet-apply` | Apply chezmoi update to all configured hosts in parallel | `scripts/fleet/apply.py` |
| `fleet-edit` | Edit fleet inventory (~/.config/fleet/machines.toml) | (builtin; seeds template) |
| `fleet-status` | Pre-flight readiness probe (up-to-date/behind/drift/busy/...) | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --readiness` |
| `fleet-status-quick` | Like fleet-status but skip remote git fetch | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --readiness --readiness-no-fetch` |
| `fleet-apply-dry-run` | Preview: run chezmoi diff on every host (no changes) | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --dry-run` |
| `fleet-diff HOST` | Quick chezmoi diff against ONE host, serial output | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --dry-run --hosts --serial` |
| `fleet-apply-file PATH` | Apply ONLY a single chezmoi target on each host (vibe loop) | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --apply-only-path` |
| `fleet-apply-branch BRANCH` | Apply a feature BRANCH instead of pulling main | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --branch` |
| `fleet-apply-branch-force BRANCH` | Same but with git reset --hard on remotes | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --branch --force-checkout` |
| `fleet-apply-one HOST` | Apply to single host in --serial mode (debug-friendly) | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --hosts --serial` |
| `fleet-apply-kill` | Kill orphan chezmoi/ansible processes on every host | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --kill-orphans` |
| `fleet-apply-status` | Probe each host for running chezmoi/ansible | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --status` |
| `fleet-apply-watch` | Re-poll every 10s until everyone idle | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --status --watch 10` |
| `fleet-apply-tail HOST` | Live-tail the remote fleet-apply log of HOST | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --tail` |
| `fleet-apply-compact` | Post-mortem summary (final task, runtime, slow tasks, exit code) | `scripts/fleet/apply.py --compact` |

### 2. **Fleet Documentation Style**

**`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`** — Uses a **three-layer table** organizational pattern:
- **Section headings**: "The fleet-* command family at a glance" (table with Recipe / What it does / Side effects / When to use)
- **Typical workflows** — bash example blocks (e.g., `git push → just fleet-status → just fleet-apply`)
- **Umbrella `fleet` binary** — separate section with mapping table (`fleet chezmoi <action>` → `just fleet-*` recipe equivalence)

**`docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`** — Structured as:
- **Install** section (auto-deployed)
- **Three execution modes** (table: Default / --shell / --login / --no-augment-path)
- **Combinations** (code block examples)
- **PATH augmentation** (explanation with prelude order)
- **AI summary mode** (Tier / Glyph / Meaning table + example output)

**Yes, tv is prominent:**
- Custom channels live in `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/*.toml` (~37 channel files)
- **Not mentioned in fleet docs** but referenced in `docs/tools/tv.md` + `docs/tools/tv-vs-fzf.md`
- **No `docs/tools/television.md`** — use `docs/tools/tv.md` instead
- **Cabinet organization**: Channels are `.toml` files organized by domain (agent-panes, ansible, audit-events, clash, disk, firewall, lan-devices, mlflow, pueue, sesh, sessions, skills, sms, ssh-config, sudo-history, super-productivity, tools, users, etc.)
- **lan-scan.sh** — `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/executable_lan-scan.sh` powers the `lan-devices` channel with nmap + arp scanning

### 4. **Existing Pickers**

**No fzf, gum, or skim found in fleet scripts or `dot_dotfiles/bin/`.**

Primary picker integration:

- **fzf** — used for shell history (`Ctrl+R`), file completion (`Ctrl+T`), directory cd (`Alt+C`); config at `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/tools/10_fzf.zsh` (no fleet integration)
- **gum** — mentioned in `docs/tools/gum.md` but no active use in fleet/scripts

**Fleet scripts** (`scripts/fleet/*.py`) use **argparse** (no interactive pickers), routing all UX through `--hosts`, `--json`, `--ai` flags instead.

231	Subcommands under `fleet chezmoi`:

234	  status --quick   Skip remote git fetch
235	  status --live    Process-liveness probe

238	  kill             pkill chezmoi/ansible across the fleet

243	def _dispatch_chezmoi(forwarded: list[str]) -> int:
244	    """Route `fleet chezmoi <action> [args...]` to the chezmoi-backend helpers.
245	
246	    The top-level `apply`/`status`/`diff`/`tail`/`kill`/`compact` subcommands
247	    were removed on 2026-05-13 to free the top level for generic primitives
248	    (`tmux` / `info` / `pueue` / `exec`). All chezmoi-specific deploy ops
249	    live under this namespace now.
250	    """
251	    if not forwarded or forwarded[0] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
252	        print(_CHEZMOI_ACTIONS)
253	        return 0
254	    action = forwarded[0]
255	    rest = forwarded[1:]
256	    nested = {
257	        "apply": _dispatch_apply,
258	        "status": _dispatch_status,
259	        "diff": _dispatch_diff,
260	        "tail": _dispatch_tail,
261	        "kill": _dispatch_kill,
262	        "compact": _dispatch_compact,
263	    }
264	    fn = nested.get(action)
265	    if fn is None:
266	        print(f"fleet chezmoi: unknown action '{action}'\n\n{_CHEZMOI_ACTIONS}", file=sys.stderr)
267	        return 2
268	    return fn(rest)

286	        # removed on 2026-05-13 — `fleet apply` now errors with "unknown
287	        # subcommand" by design so the namespace stays clean.
288	        "chezmoi": _dispatch_chezmoi,

292	        "tmux": _dispatch_tmux,
293	        "info": _dispatch_info,
294	        "pueue": _dispatch_pueue,
295	        "exec": _dispatch_exec,
296	    }
297	    fn = dispatch.get(sub)
298	    if fn is None:
299	        print(f"fleet: unknown subcommand '{sub}'\n\n{USAGE}", file=sys.stderr)
300	        return 2

103	def load_hosts(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Host], dict]:
104	    """Parse machines.toml -> ([Host, ...], defaults dict).
105	
106	    Merges [defaults] into each host (host overrides defaults). The
107	    `password_source` table is normalized into (type, arg) on Host.
108	    """
109	    if not path.exists():
110	        raise FileNotFoundError(
111	            f"Fleet config not found: {path}\n"
112	            f"Hint: chezmoi apply seeds ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — edit it "
113	            f"to list your machines, or pass --config PATH."
114	        )
115	    with path.open("rb") as f:
116	        data = tomllib.load(f)
117	
118	    defaults = data.get("defaults", {}) or {}
119	    raw_hosts = data.get("hosts", []) or []
120	    if not raw_hosts:
121	        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no [[hosts]] entries defined.")
122	
123	    hosts: list[Host] = []
124	    seen_names: set[str] = set()
125	    for idx, raw in enumerate(raw_hosts):
126	        name = raw.get("name")
127	        if not name:
128	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: [[hosts]][{idx}] missing required `name`.")
129	        if name in seen_names:
130	            raise ValueError(f"{path}: duplicate host name {name!r}.")
131	        seen_names.add(name)
132	
133	        merged = {**defaults, **raw}

135	        ps_type = (ps.get("type") or "none").lower()
136	        if ps_type not in ("plain", "prompt", "bitwarden", "none"):

143	        host_fields = {f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(Host)}
144	        host_kwargs = {k: v for k, v in merged.items() if k in host_fields}
145	        host = Host(

558	def _connect_kwargs(host: Host) -> dict:
559	    """Translate Host -> asyncssh.connect kwargs.
560	
561	    asyncssh reads ~/.ssh/config by default for the `host` arg. When ssh_alias
562	    is set we pass it as `host` and let asyncssh resolve hostname/user/port/
563	    IdentityFile/ProxyJump from ssh_config. Explicit fields override.
564	    """
565	    target = host.ssh_alias or host.hostname
566	    assert target is not None  # validated in load_hosts
567	    kwargs: dict = {"host": target, "known_hosts": None}
568	    # known_hosts=None tells asyncssh to skip its own check; we still rely on
569	    # the user having ssh'd manually first (StrictHostKeyChecking is enforced
570	    # implicitly by them adding it to ~/.ssh/known_hosts ahead of time).
571	    # Switching to known_hosts=() would force strict but reject every new host.
572	    if host.user:
573	        kwargs["username"] = host.user
574	    if host.port:
575	        kwargs["port"] = host.port
576	    if host.identity_file:
577	        kwargs["client_keys"] = [str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]

583

585	    Silent on errors (best-effort cleanup).
586	    """
587	    if keep <= 0:
588	        return
589	    try:
590	        logs = sorted(
591	            LOCAL_LOG_DIR.glob("*.log"),
592	            key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime,
593	            reverse=True,
594	        )
595	    except OSError:
596	        return
597	    for stale in logs[keep:]:
598	        for ext in (".log", ".exit"):
599	            try:

601	            except OSError:

# `fleet hosts` — interactive picker for SSH'ing into fleet-configured machines

## Context

The fleet inventory at `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` is the SSOT for every cross-host operation (`fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`). Today you can introspect it indirectly (each command's `--hosts` flag) but there is no quick "give me a picker, let me pick one, SSH me in" path. Meanwhile `dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml` already gives exactly that UX for `~/.ssh/config` via `tv ssh-config` — but fleet hosts live in TOML, not `~/.ssh/config`, and some have explicit `hostname` / `user` / `port` / `identity_file` instead of an `ssh_alias`, so a fleet-aware picker is needed.

**Outcome**: a new `tv fleet-hosts` cable (analog to `tv ssh-config`) and a `fleet hosts` umbrella subcommand backed by `scripts/fleet/hosts.py`. The Python module is the SSOT for inventory listing/preview/connect — the TV cable shells out to it, so there is no duplicate TOML parser. Direct CLI usage (`fleet hosts lab-box` to SSH straight in, `fleet hosts --list` for scripts) also works without `tv`.

## Architecture

\```
~/.config/fleet/machines.toml   (existing SSOT)
            │
            ▼
scripts/fleet/hosts.py          (new — uses load_hosts() from apply.py)
            │   subcommand verbs:
            │     --list                       plain names, one per line
            │     --list-tsv                   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind     (TV source)
            │     --list-json                  full inventory JSON
            │     --describe NAME              preview text                (TV preview)
            │     --probe NAME                 BatchMode SSH probe         (Alt+T action)
            │     <NAME>                       SSH connect directly (os.execvp)
            │     (no args)                    exec `tv fleet-hosts`; fallback: numeric menu
            │
            ├──────────────────────────┐
            ▼                          ▼
dot_config/television/cable/   dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet
   fleet-hosts.toml              ("hosts" added to dispatch)
   (TV cable — shells out to
    `fleet hosts --list-tsv`
    `fleet hosts --describe`
    `fleet hosts <NAME>`)
\```

## Files to create

### 1. `scripts/fleet/hosts.py` (new)

PEP 723 inline-deps Python module. Uses `tomllib` (stdlib, py>=3.11) — does NOT need `asyncssh` / `rich` / `tyro`. Imports `load_hosts`, `Host`, `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` from `scripts.fleet` (re-exported via `__init__.py`).

Argparse skeleton:

\```python
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = []  # stdlib only
# ///
"""fleet hosts — pick a fleet host, SSH in."""
from scripts.fleet import DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH, Host, load_hosts

# Modes (mutually exclusive, dispatched in order):
#   --list / --list-tsv / --list-json        → print, exit 0
#   --describe NAME                          → print preview block, exit 0
#   --probe NAME                             → run ssh -o BatchMode=yes ... true
#   <NAME positional>                        → os.execvp("ssh", [...])
#   (no args) and tv on PATH                 → os.execvp("tv", ["tv", "fleet-hosts"])
#   (no args) and no tv                      → numeric stdin menu fallback

def _ssh_argv(host: Host) -> list[str]:
    """Build argv for `ssh ...` matching _connect_kwargs() semantics."""
    if host.ssh_alias:
        return ["ssh", host.ssh_alias]
    # Explicit fields path
    argv = ["ssh"]
    if host.port:        argv += ["-p", str(host.port)]
    if host.identity_file: argv += ["-i", str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
    target = f"{host.user}@{host.hostname}" if host.user else host.hostname
    argv.append(target)
    return argv

def _kind(host: Host) -> str:
    if host.local:       return "LOCAL"
    if host.ssh_alias:   return f"alias:{host.ssh_alias}"
    parts = [host.hostname or "?"]
    if host.port and host.port != 22: parts.append(f":{host.port}")
    return f"explicit:{host.user + '@' if host.user else ''}{''.join(parts)}"
\```

**`--describe NAME` output** (preview pane — multi-section, plain text):

\```
# host: lab-box        (defined in: ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)

connection:
  ssh_alias       lab-box
  user            (from ssh_config)
  hostname        (from ssh_config)
  port            (from ssh_config)
  identity_file   (from ssh_config)

fleet metadata:
  local                false
  no_root_machine      false
  chezmoi_path         auto
  password_source      bitwarden (item=ssh-lab-box-sudo)
  extra_env            (none)

ssh -G resolution (if ssh_alias present):
  hostname 192.0.2.42
  user dwlee
  port 22
  identityfile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
  proxyjump bastion.example.com

local key check:
  [OK]   ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
\```

`ssh -G` block is omitted for explicit-fields hosts. **Never print `password_source_arg` for type=plain** — only show the type label.

**`local = true` hosts**:
- Included in `--list` / `--list-json` (scriptable consumers may want them).
- **Excluded** from `--list-tsv` (TV cable source) by default, so the picker never shows you yourself. A `--include-local` flag overrides for completeness.
- `fleet hosts <name>` on a `local` host: print `"fleet hosts: '<name>' is local = true — nothing to SSH into"` and exit 0.

**No-args dispatch**:
1. If `shutil.which("tv")`: `os.execvp("tv", ["tv", "fleet-hosts"])`.
2. Else: enumerate non-local hosts, print a numbered list, read stdin, dispatch to SSH. This is a *safety net* for headless CI; on every dev machine `tv` is installed via the devtools role.

### 2. `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` (new)

Modeled directly on `ssh-config.toml` but sourced from `fleet hosts`. Schema:

\```toml
[metadata]
name = "fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]

[source]
command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
# e.g.   lab-box	lab-box	alias:lab-box
display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
output  = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:connect"
alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-s = "actions:status"
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:pueue"

[actions.connect]
description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login work?)"
command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.status]
description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"
command = "fleet chezmoi status --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.info]
description = "fleet info for this host"
command = "fleet info --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.pueue]
description = "fleet pueue for this host"
command = "fleet pueue --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
\```

**Header comment** at the top (matching ssh-config.toml's style) documents: source SSOT, keybindings, and the "tv = picker, fleet hosts CLI = direct/scriptable" duality.

## Reused functions (do NOT reimplement)

- `scripts.fleet.load_hosts(path)` → returns `(list[Host], defaults_dict)`. Already validates `name` uniqueness and `ssh_alias OR hostname OR local`.
- `scripts.fleet.Host` dataclass → fields `name`, `ssh_alias`, `hostname`, `user`, `port`, `identity_file`, `local`, `no_root_machine`, `chezmoi_path`, `extra_env`, `password_source_type`, `password_source_arg`.
- `scripts.fleet.DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` → respects `FLEET_CONFIG` env var override.
- `scripts.fleet._connect_kwargs(host)` → **NOT used directly** (it builds asyncssh kwargs). Mirror its precedence logic in the new `_ssh_argv()` helper (ssh_alias wins over explicit fields), keeping the two in semantic lockstep.
- `chezmoi source-path` discovery → already done by `executable_fleet`'s `_source_path()`; `hosts.py` runs inside the same process via `from scripts.fleet.hosts import main`, so `sys.path` is already set.

## Design decisions / tradeoffs

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| TOML parser | `tomllib` (stdlib) | py>=3.11 is already required by every other fleet module. No extra deps. |
| Picker engine | TV cable | Matches the user's stated analogy with `tv ssh-config`. Free preview/keybinding UX. |
| Inventory parsing for the cable | shells out to `fleet hosts --list-tsv` | One SSOT (Python `load_hosts`); the cable stays a thin TOML config, no inline TOML parsing. |
| Direct invocation | `fleet hosts NAME` → `os.execvp("ssh", ...)` | Replaces the shell with ssh — the user's terminal is now an interactive SSH session, exactly as they'd expect. |
| `local = true` hosts | Hidden from picker, shown by `--list`/`--list-json` | SSH'ing into yourself is silly, but scripts that want full inventory still see them. |
| `password_source` in preview | Show type only (never `arg` for `plain`) | The TOML file itself is 0600 but preview output may scroll into other logs/screenshots. Defence in depth. |
| Action keys | `Enter` / `Alt+T` / `Alt+S` / `Alt+I` / `Alt+P` | Mirrors `ssh-config.toml`'s `Alt+` namespace (CLAUDE.md keybinding rule: avoid `Ctrl+letter` collisions with tmux). |
| No `Ctrl+E` "fleet exec" action | Out of scope | `fleet exec` needs a command string — picker can't prompt for arbitrary argv. Add later if needed. |

## Out of scope (deliberately deferred)

- A picker-driven `fleet exec` (would need a command-input modal — TV cable can't prompt).
- `Alt+L` to "live-tail" a host's `fleet chezmoi apply` log — possible later via `fleet chezmoi tail`.
- Multi-select then fan-out (e.g. pick 3 hosts → `fleet exec` on those). TV is single-select; deferred to a Python TUI if ever wanted.
- A `justfile` recipe wrapping `fleet hosts` — both `fleet hosts` and `tv fleet-hosts` are short enough; recipes don't add value here.
- `~/.shellrc.adhoc` alias suggestions (e.g. `alias fh='fleet hosts'`) — leave to the user.

## Reused functions (do NOT reimplement)

- `scripts.fleet.load_hosts(path)` → returns `(list[Host], defaults_dict)`. Already validates `name` uniqueness and `ssh_alias OR hostname OR local`.
- `scripts.fleet.Host` dataclass → fields `name`, `ssh_alias`, `hostname`, `user`, `port`, `identity_file`, `local`, `no_root_machine`, `chezmoi_path`, `extra_env`, `password_source_type`, `password_source_arg`.
- `scripts.fleet.DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` → respects `FLEET_CONFIG` env var override.
- `scripts.fleet._connect_kwargs(host)` → **NOT used directly** (it builds asyncssh kwargs). Mirror its precedence logic in the new `_ssh_argv()` helper (ssh_alias wins over explicit fields), keeping the two in semantic lockstep.
- `chezmoi source-path` discovery → already done by `executable_fleet`'s `_source_path()`; `hosts.py` runs inside the same process via `from scripts.fleet.hosts import main`, so `sys.path` is already set.

## Design decisions / tradeoffs

| Decision | Choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| TOML parser | `tomllib` (stdlib) | py>=3.11 is already required by every other fleet module. No extra deps. |
| Picker engine | TV cable | Matches the user's stated analogy with `tv ssh-config`. Free preview/keybinding UX. |
| Inventory parsing for the cable | shells out to `fleet hosts --list-tsv` | One SSOT (Python `load_hosts`); the cable stays a thin TOML config, no inline TOML parsing. |
| Direct invocation | `fleet hosts NAME` → `os.execvp("ssh", ...)` | Replaces the shell with ssh — the user's terminal is now an interactive SSH session, exactly as they'd expect. |
| `local = true` hosts | Hidden from picker, shown by `--list`/`--list-json` | SSH'ing into yourself is silly, but scripts that want full inventory still see them. |
| `password_source` in preview | Show type only (never `arg` for `plain`) | The TOML file itself is 0600 but preview output may scroll into other logs/screenshots. Defence in depth. |
| Action keys | `Enter` / `Alt+T` / `Alt+S` / `Alt+I` / `Alt+P` | Mirrors `ssh-config.toml`'s `Alt+` namespace (CLAUDE.md keybinding rule: avoid `Ctrl+letter` collisions with tmux). |
| No `Ctrl+E` "fleet exec" action | Out of scope | `fleet exec` needs a command string — picker can't prompt for arbitrary argv. Add later if needed. |

5. **Probe mode** (used by Alt+T):

   ```

6. **TV cable** (full UX):
   ```bash

   chezmoi apply ~/.config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = []
# ///
"""fleet hosts — pick a fleet-configured host, SSH into it.

Three entry points:

  fleet hosts                 Interactive picker via `tv fleet-hosts`. Falls
                              back to a numbered-stdin menu if `tv` is not on
                              PATH (e.g. headless CI).
  fleet hosts NAME            SSH directly into NAME (skip the picker). Uses
                              ssh_alias if set; otherwise constructs
                              `ssh -p PORT -i KEY user@hostname`.
  fleet hosts --list*         Script-friendly inventory dumps — also used by
                              the TV cable + your own shell glue:
                                --list        plain names, one per line
                                --list-tsv    name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
                                --list-json   full inventory JSON
                                --describe N  preview block for N
                                --probe N     BatchMode SSH probe of N

Mirrors `dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml` (which is sourced from
~/.ssh/config), but reads ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml instead so explicit
hostname/user/port/identity_file hosts (no ssh_config alias) are reachable.

The TV cable at `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` shells out to
`fleet hosts --list-tsv` (source), `fleet hosts --describe '{...}'` (preview),
and `fleet hosts '{...}'` (Enter action). This module is the SSOT for fleet
inventory introspection — the only TOML parser is `load_hosts()` in apply.py.

`local = true` hosts are hidden from `--list-tsv` (picker) by default — SSH'ing
into yourself is silly. Use `--include-local` to override, or run
`fleet hosts NAME` on a local host (prints a no-op message and exits 0).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import dataclasses
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Bootstrap: when invoked directly (not via the `fleet hosts` dispatcher in
# dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet), put the chezmoi source dir on sys.path
# so `from scripts.fleet import ...` works regardless of cwd.
_SRC = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent  # hosts.py -> fleet -> scripts -> src
if str(_SRC) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(_SRC))

from scripts.fleet import DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH, Host, load_hosts  # noqa: E402


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Host introspection helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _kind(host: Host) -> str:
    """Compact connection-style summary for the picker's 3rd column."""
    if host.local:
        return "LOCAL"
    if host.ssh_alias:
        return f"alias:{host.ssh_alias}"
    parts: list[str] = []
    if host.user:
        parts.append(f"{host.user}@")
    parts.append(host.hostname or "?")
    if host.port and host.port != 22:
        parts.append(f":{host.port}")
    return "explicit:" + "".join(parts)


def _target(host: Host) -> str:
    """Resolved SSH target for the picker's 2nd column."""
    if host.local:
        return "(local)"
    if host.ssh_alias:
        return host.ssh_alias
    return host.hostname or "?"


def _ssh_argv(host: Host) -> list[str]:
    """argv for `ssh ...`. Mirrors apply.py:_connect_kwargs precedence —
    ssh_alias wins (let ssh_config resolve everything); otherwise build from
    hostname/user/port/identity_file."""
    if host.ssh_alias:
        return ["ssh", host.ssh_alias]
    argv: list[str] = ["ssh"]
    if host.port:
        argv += ["-p", str(host.port)]
    if host.identity_file:
        argv += ["-i", str(Path(host.identity_file).expanduser())]
    target = f"{host.user}@{host.hostname}" if host.user else (host.hostname or "")
    argv.append(target)
    return argv


def _load(config: Path) -> list[Host]:
    try:
        hosts, _defaults = load_hosts(config)
    except (FileNotFoundError, ValueError) as e:
        print(f"fleet hosts: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    return hosts


def _find_host(name: str, hosts: list[Host]) -> Host:
    for h in hosts:
        if h.name == name:
            return h
    available = ", ".join(h.name for h in hosts) or "(none)"
    print(
        f"fleet hosts: unknown host {name!r}. Available: {available}",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    sys.exit(2)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Listing modes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _cmd_list_plain(hosts: list[Host]) -> int:
    for h in hosts:
        print(h.name)
    return 0


def _cmd_list_tsv(hosts: list[Host], include_local: bool) -> int:
    for h in hosts:
        if h.local and not include_local:
            continue
        print(f"{h.name}\t{_target(h)}\t{_kind(h)}")
    return 0


def _cmd_list_json(hosts: list[Host], config: Path) -> int:
    payload = []
    for h in hosts:
        d = dataclasses.asdict(h)
        # Never leak a resolved sudo_password (it'd be None at this point —
        # resolve_passwords() never ran — but be defensive in case that
        # changes).
        d.pop("sudo_password", None)
        # For plain-type password sources, the TOML file itself is 0600 but
        # JSON dump goes to stdout (could be piped into logs/screenshots).
        if d.get("password_source_type") == "plain":
            d["password_source_arg"] = "(redacted — type=plain)"
        payload.append(d)
    json.dump(
        {"config": str(config), "hosts": payload},
        sys.stdout,
        indent=2,
        default=str,
    )
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Describe (TV preview pane)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _ssh_g_lines(alias: str, wanted: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[str]:
    """Run `ssh -G ALIAS` and return matching `key value` lines."""
    if not shutil.which("ssh"):
        return []
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["ssh", "-G", alias],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=3,
            check=False,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return []
    if out.returncode != 0:
        return []
    matched: list[str] = []
    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
        parts = line.split(None, 1)
        if len(parts) == 2 and parts[0] in wanted:
            matched.append(line)
    return matched


def _identity_paths_from_ssh_g(alias: str) -> list[str]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for line in _ssh_g_lines(alias, ("identityfile",)):
        parts = line.split(None, 1)
        if len(parts) == 2:
            out.append(parts[1])
    return out


def _expand_key_path(p: str) -> Path:
    return Path(p.replace("~", str(Path.home()))).expanduser()


def _cmd_describe(name: str, hosts: list[Host], config: Path) -> int:
    h = _find_host(name, hosts)

    print(f"# host: {h.name}        (defined in: {config})")
    print()

    print("connection:")
    if h.local:
        print("  local           true   (runs on orchestrator — no SSH)")
    elif h.ssh_alias:
        print(f"  ssh_alias       {h.ssh_alias}")
        print(f"  user            {h.user or '(from ssh_config)'}")
        print(f"  hostname        {h.hostname or '(from ssh_config)'}")
        print(f"  port            {h.port if h.port is not None else '(from ssh_config)'}")
        print(f"  identity_file   {h.identity_file or '(from ssh_config)'}")
    else:
        print("  ssh_alias       (none — explicit fields below)")
        print(f"  user            {h.user or '(default)'}")
        print(f"  hostname        {h.hostname}")
        print(f"  port            {h.port if h.port is not None else 22}")
        print(f"  identity_file   {h.identity_file or '(default agent / key)'}")
    print()

    print("fleet metadata:")
    print(f"  local                {str(h.local).lower()}")
    print(f"  no_root_machine      {str(h.no_root_machine).lower()}")
    print(f"  chezmoi_path         {h.chezmoi_path}")
    ps_label = h.password_source_type
    if h.password_source_arg and h.password_source_type != "plain":
        ps_label += f" (item={h.password_source_arg})"
    elif h.password_source_type == "plain":
        ps_label += " (value redacted)"
    print(f"  password_source      {ps_label}")
    if h.extra_env:
        print(f"  extra_env            {', '.join(h.extra_env.keys())}")
    else:
        print("  extra_env            (none)")
    print()

    if h.ssh_alias:
        print(f"ssh -G {h.ssh_alias!r} (resolved by ssh_config):")
        wanted = (
            "hostname", "user", "port", "identityfile",
            "proxycommand", "proxyjump", "forwardagent", "identityagent",
        )
        lines = _ssh_g_lines(h.ssh_alias, wanted)
        if not lines:
            print("  (ssh -G unavailable or returned nothing)")
        else:
            for line in lines:
                print(f"  {line}")
        print()

    if not h.local:
        print("local key check (offline):")
        paths: list[str] = []
        if h.identity_file:
            paths.append(h.identity_file)
        elif h.ssh_alias:
            paths = _identity_paths_from_ssh_g(h.ssh_alias)
        if not paths:
            print("  (no identityfile to check)")
        else:
            found = False
            for p in paths:
                f = _expand_key_path(p)
                if f.is_file():
                    print(f"  [OK]   {f}")
                    found = True
                else:
                    print(f"  [miss] {f}")
            if not found:
                print()
                print(
                    "  => no IdentityFile present locally —"
                    " password / agent login required"
                )
        print()

    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Probe (TV Alt+T action)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _cmd_probe(name: str, hosts: list[Host]) -> int:
    h = _find_host(name, hosts)
    if h.local:
        print(f"# {h.name} is local=true — no SSH probe needed.")
        return 0
    target = h.ssh_alias or h.hostname or "?"
    print(f"# Probing {target!r} with BatchMode=yes (ConnectTimeout=3)")
    print(
        "# Exit 0 = passwordless login works; non-zero = needs password /"
        " key not authorized / unreachable"
    )
    print()

    argv = _ssh_argv(h)
    argv = [
        argv[0],
        "-o", "BatchMode=yes",
        "-o", "ConnectTimeout=3",
        "-o", "StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new",
        "-o", "PreferredAuthentications=publickey,hostbased,gssapi-with-mic",
        *argv[1:],
        "true",
    ]
    rc = subprocess.call(argv)
    print()
    if rc == 0:
        print(f"[OK] passwordless login works for {target!r}")
    elif rc == 255:
        print("[FAIL] connection / auth error (exit 255) — needs password,"
              " key not authorized, or host unreachable")
    else:
        print(f"[FAIL] remote command failed (exit {rc}) — auth probably OK"
              " but 'true' failed")
    return rc


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Direct SSH (positional NAME)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _cmd_connect(name: str, hosts: list[Host]) -> int:
    h = _find_host(name, hosts)
    if h.local:
        print(
            f"fleet hosts: '{h.name}' is local = true — nothing to SSH into "
            "(you're already on the orchestrator).",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 0
    argv = _ssh_argv(h)
    # os.execvp replaces this process with ssh, so the user's terminal
    # becomes the SSH session directly — matches Enter in `tv ssh-config`.
    try:
        os.execvp(argv[0], argv)
    except OSError as e:
        print(f"fleet hosts: failed to exec {argv[0]}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 127
    return 0  # unreachable


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Picker (no args)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _cmd_picker(hosts: list[Host]) -> int:
    tv = shutil.which("tv")
    if tv:
        try:
            os.execvp(tv, [tv, "fleet-hosts"])
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"fleet hosts: failed to exec tv: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            # fall through to text menu

    pickable = [h for h in hosts if not h.local]
    if not pickable:
        print(
            "fleet hosts: no SSH-able hosts in inventory (all `local = true`).",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    print("Fleet hosts (pick one to SSH into):")
    for i, h in enumerate(pickable, 1):
        print(f"  {i:>2}. {h.name:<24}  {_kind(h)}")
    print()
    try:
        choice = input("Number (or empty to abort): ").strip()
    except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
        print()
        return 130
    if not choice:
        return 0
    try:
        idx = int(choice) - 1
        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(pickable):
            raise ValueError
    except ValueError:
        print(f"fleet hosts: invalid choice {choice!r}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    return _cmd_connect(pickable[idx].name, hosts)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="fleet hosts",
        description=(
            "Pick a fleet-configured host and SSH in. Mirrors `tv ssh-config`,"
            " but sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml."
        ),
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "name",
        nargs="?",
        help="Host name to SSH into (skip the picker). Use `--list` to enumerate.",
    )
    modes = p.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    modes.add_argument(
        "--list",
        action="store_true",
        help="Plain host names, one per line.",
    )
    modes.add_argument(
        "--list-tsv",
        action="store_true",
        dest="list_tsv",
        help="TSV `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` (used by the TV cable source).",
    )
    modes.add_argument(
        "--list-json",
        action="store_true",
        dest="list_json",
        help="Full inventory as JSON (plain password values are redacted).",
    )
    modes.add_argument(
        "--describe",
        metavar="NAME",
        help="Print the preview block for NAME (used by the TV cable preview).",
    )
    modes.add_argument(
        "--probe",
        metavar="NAME",
        help="BatchMode SSH probe of NAME (used by the TV cable Alt+T action).",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--include-local",
        action="store_true",
        help="Include `local = true` hosts in --list-tsv (default: hidden).",
    )
    p.add_argument(
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH,
        help=f"Fleet inventory path (default: {DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH}).",
    )
    return p


def main() -> int:
    args = _build_parser().parse_args()
    hosts = _load(args.config)

    if args.list:
        return _cmd_list_plain(hosts)
    if args.list_tsv:
        return _cmd_list_tsv(hosts, include_local=args.include_local)
    if args.list_json:
        return _cmd_list_json(hosts, args.config)
    if args.describe:
        return _cmd_describe(args.describe, hosts, args.config)
    if args.probe:
        return _cmd_probe(args.probe, hosts)
    if args.name:
        return _cmd_connect(args.name, hosts)
    return _cmd_picker(hosts)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

```toml
# Custom fleet-hosts channel for television (tv).
# Sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — the same inventory used by
# `fleet chezmoi apply` / `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` /
# `fleet exec`. Mirrors the `ssh-config` cable's UX but reads fleet's TOML
# inventory instead of ~/.ssh/config, so hosts with explicit
# hostname/user/port/identity_file (no ssh_alias) are reachable too.
#
# The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to:
#   fleet hosts --list-tsv      (source — `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` lines)
#   fleet hosts --describe N    (preview pane content)
#   fleet hosts N               (Enter action — os.execvp("ssh", ...))
# So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes
# automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync).
#
# Usage:
#   tv fleet-hosts
#   fleet hosts          # same picker via the fleet umbrella
#   fleet hosts lab-box  # skip the picker, SSH directly
#
# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
#   Enter      SSH into the selected host
#   Alt+T      BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login actually work?)
#   Alt+S      fleet chezmoi status scoped to this host
#   Alt+I      fleet info scoped to this host
#   Alt+P      fleet pueue scoped to this host
#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
#
# `local = true` hosts are intentionally hidden — they live on the
# orchestrator and have no SSH endpoint. Run `fleet hosts --list-tsv
# --include-local` to confirm one is in the inventory.

[metadata]
name = "fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]

[source]
command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
# e.g.   lab-box <TAB> lab-box <TAB> alias:lab-box
#        vps-tokyo <TAB> 203.0.113.42 <TAB> explicit:dwlee@203.0.113.42
display = "{split:\t:0}  ({split:\t:2})"
output = "{split:\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:connect"
alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-s = "actions:status"
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:pueue"

[actions.connect]
description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
command = "fleet hosts '{split:\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.status]
description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"
command = "fleet chezmoi status --hosts '{split:\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.info]
description = "fleet info for this host"
command = "fleet info --hosts '{split:\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

[actions.pueue]
description = "fleet pueue for this host"
command = "fleet pueue --hosts '{split:\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"

```

```text
1	# fleet exec — cross-host ad-hoc command runner
2	
3	`fleet exec` runs an arbitrary command across every host in your fleet
4	inventory (`~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`), collects per-host stdout +
5	stderr + exit code, and renders a table — optionally with an AI-summarised
6	classification (succeeded / differed / failed).
7	
8	Sister tools: [`fleet pueue`](pueue.md) for structured queue probing,
9	[`fleet tmux`](../this_repo/fleet-apply.md#fleet-tmux--cross-host-tmux-session-summary)
10	for tmux session summaries, [`fleet info`](../this_repo/fleet-apply.md)
11	for system metadata snapshots. All four share the same asyncssh + semaphore
12	plumbing from `scripts/fleet/apply.py`.
13	
14	## Install
15	
16	Deployed automatically by chezmoi as part of the `fleet` umbrella:
17	
18	- `~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet` — the umbrella binary
19	- `~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/fleet/exec.py` — the implementation
20	  (resolved at runtime via `chezmoi source-path`)
21	
22	No separate install step.
23	
24	## Three execution modes (orthogonal flags)
25	
26	The `--shell` / `--login` / `--no-augment-path` flags are independent and
27	compose freely. Defaults bias for safety (no shell expansion) and speed
28	(no rc-file load).
29	
30	| Mode | Wire format | When to use |
31	|------|-------------|-------------|
32	| **Default (argv list)** | `<argv shlex-quoted>` via `sh -c` on remote | Most ad-hoc commands. No globs, pipes, or `$VAR` expansion. Safe by construction. |
33	| `--shell bash` | `bash -c '<argv space-joined>'` | When you need pipes (`\|`), globs (`*`), redirects (`>`), `&&`/`;` chains, or `$VAR` interpolation. |
34	| `--shell zsh` | `zsh -c '<...>'` | Zsh-specific syntax (`${(...)}`, `=~`, etc.). |
35	| `--login` | `bash -lc '<quoted argv>'` (or `<shell> -lc`) | Tools needing rc-loaded env: `nvm`, `mise`, `pyenv`, `conda activate`, shell aliases/functions. Slower (~150-500ms rc-load per host). |
36	| `--no-augment-path` | Direct argv, no PATH prelude | Debugging "what does SSH see by default" on this host. Mutually exclusive with `--login`. |
37	
38	Combinations:
39	
40	```bash
41	fleet exec -- pueue --version                       # argv default
42	fleet exec --shell bash -- 'cat *.log | grep ERR'   # shell for pipe + glob
43	fleet exec --login -- pueue --version               # rc-loaded env
44	fleet exec --login --shell zsh -- 'conda activate myenv && python -V'
45	fleet exec --no-augment-path -- echo "\$PATH"       # raw SSH PATH
46	```
47	
48	`--` is the standard wrapper-CLI separator (same pattern as `ssh`, `docker
49	run`, `cargo run`, `pytest`). Everything after `--` is opaque to fleet's
50	own option parser, so inner-command flags like `--version` or `-c` never
51	collide with fleet's flags.
52	
53	## PATH augmentation
54	
55	Like [`fleet pueue`](pueue.md), this command prepends a fixed PATH prelude
56	on every host so user-installed binaries are visible to the
57	non-interactive SSH shell:
58	
59	```
60	~/.dotfiles/bin → ~/.cargo/bin → ~/.local/bin → ~/bin →
61	/opt/homebrew/bin → /usr/local/bin → /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin →
62	~/.linuxbrew/bin → $PATH
63	```
64	
65	Order favours package-manager dirs (`~/.cargo/bin`, `~/.local/bin`) over
66	legacy `~/bin` so a stale download in `~/bin` doesn't shadow a fresher
67	`cargo install` of the same tool. `--no-augment-path` skips the prelude;
68	`--login` bypasses it (login shells load PATH from rc files instead).
69	
70	This is a known divergence from your interactive shell's PATH order — see
71	[pueue.md § PATH augmentation](pueue.md) for the full rationale.
72	
73	## AI summary mode
74	
75	`fleet exec --ai` pipes the merged per-host JSON through the configured
76	LLM agent (`opencode` → `claude` → `codex` → `cursor-agent` priority, per
77	`dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh`). The LLM classifies each host:
78	
79	| Tier | Glyph | Meaning |
80	|------|-------|---------|
81	| `succeeded` | 🟢 | rc=0 AND stdout matches cluster majority |
82	| `differed` | 🟡 | rc=0 BUT stdout meaningfully differs (version drift, config drift, OS-specific output) |
83	| `failed` | 🔴 | rc≠0 OR SSH/timeout error |
84	
85	Example output:
86	
87	```
88	🌐 4 hosts on pueue 4.0.2, ts_nas lagging on 4.0.1 — consider upgrading NAS
89	
90	majority: pueue 4.0.2
91	
92	🟢 succeeded (4)
93	  self            rc=0     pueue 4.0.2 — matches cluster majority
94	  hanru_mac       rc=0     pueue 4.0.2 — matches cluster majority
95	  jingle207       rc=0     pueue 4.0.2 — matches cluster majority
96	  david_ubuntu    rc=0     pueue 4.0.2 — matches cluster majority
97	
98	🟡 differed (1)
99	  ts_nas          rc=0     pueue 4.0.1 — one minor version behind
100	```
101	
102	### Markdown reports
103	
104	`fleet exec --ai --report --out PATH` emits a markdown document with
105	Summary / Succeeded / Differed / Failed sections plus per-host raw outputs
106	in a collapsible details block. Useful for sharing audit results, dropping
107	into commit messages, or archiving point-in-time fleet snapshots.
108	
109	### Cache
110	
111	Results cache at `~/.cache/fleet-exec/<host>-<prompt_hash>.json` (TTL
112	`FLEETEXEC_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL` seconds, default 120). The cache key is a
113	SHA of `(prompt + per-host stdout/stderr/rc)` — `elapsed_ms` is excluded
114	from the hash so identical command outputs reuse cache regardless of SSH
115	timing variance.
116	
117	Force refresh: `fleet exec --ai --refresh -- ...`.
118	Skip cache entirely: `fleet exec --ai --no-cache -- ...`.
119	Inspect what would be sent without calling the LLM: `fleet exec --ai
120	--dry-run -- ...`.
121	
122	## Output formats
123	
124	```bash
125	fleet exec -- date                       # Rich table (default)
126	fleet exec --json -- date                # JSON array of per-host records
127	fleet exec --out-dir /tmp/exec-out -- df # per-host .stdout/.stderr/.json files
128	fleet exec --full-output -- df -h /      # table + per-host blocks below
129	```
130	
131	The default table shows the **first line** of stdout, truncated to
132	terminal width. For commands with multi-line output (`df -h`, `ps -ef`,
133	`systemctl status`), `--full-output` or `--out-dir` are usually what you
134	want.
135	
136	## Subset selection
137	
138	```bash
139	fleet exec --hosts self,ts_nas -- pueue --version    # include subset
140	fleet exec --exclude jingle207 -- pueue --version    # exclude one
141	fleet exec --serial -- pueue --version               # one host at a time (debug)
142	fleet exec --max-parallel 4 -- pueue --version       # cap concurrency
143	```
144	
145	Default parallelism is `min(8, len(hosts))`. SSH connect timeout: 15s.
146	Per-command timeout: 60s (override with `--command-timeout`).
147	
148	## Exit code
149	
150	`fleet exec` exits with `min(N_failed, 125)` where `N_failed` counts hosts
151	with rc≠0 OR SSH/timeout error. Useful for CI:
152	
153	```bash
154	fleet exec --hosts production -- systemctl is-active myservice || alert.sh
155	```
156	
157	## Common audit recipes
158	
159	```bash
160	# Version drift audit
161	fleet exec --ai -- pueue --version
162	fleet exec --ai -- python3 --version
163	fleet exec --ai -- chezmoi --version
164	
165	# Disk pressure check
166	fleet exec --ai -- df -h /
167	
168	# Daemon health
169	fleet exec --shell bash -- 'systemctl --user is-active pueued 2>/dev/null || launchctl list | grep pueue'
170	
171	# Find heavyweight processes
172	fleet exec --shell bash -- 'ps aux | sort -k 4 -r | head -5'
173	
174	# Confirm a file deployed everywhere
175	fleet exec -- test -f ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml
176	
177	# Kernel audit (Linux only — macOS hosts will show "failed")
178	fleet exec --ai -- uname -r
179	```
180	
181	## Troubleshooting
182	
183	- **`not-installed` for a tool that IS installed**: the SSH non-interactive
184	  shell has a minimal PATH. `--login` should expose all user-installed
185	  tools (slower); the default PATH prelude covers the common locations
186	  but not arbitrary ones.
187	- **`bash -lc` doesn't see my conda init**: zsh-only PATH additions don't
188	  load under `bash -lc`. Use `--login --shell zsh` instead.
189	- **AI mode hangs**: `fleet exec --ai --dry-run -- ...` prints the prompt
190	  without calling the LLM. If the prompt looks fine, the issue is upstream
191	  (agent not on PATH, API key, etc.).
192	- **AI returns garbage / non-JSON**: re-run with `--refresh`; if persistent,
193	  fall back to `--json` and post-process manually.
194	- **`--clean` doesn't exist here** (unlike `pqsum ai`): `fleet exec` is for
195	  generic commands; any safety check is the user's responsibility. To
196	  delete files cluster-wide use `fleet exec --shell bash -- 'rm ...'`
197	  knowingly.
198	
199	## Cross-file invariants
200	
201	Adding new flags or changing output schemas requires touching:
202	
203	1. `scripts/fleet/exec.py` — primary implementation
204	2. `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` — USAGE block + `_dispatch_exec`
205	3. `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` — subcommand row
206	4. `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md` (+ zh-TW mirror) — this page
207	
208	When adding a new AI agent, this script becomes the 4th Python consumer
209	of `dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh` — see
210	[CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
211	AI-agent row.
212
```
</details></tool-use>

```md
# fleet hosts — picker for SSH'ing into fleet-configured machines

`fleet hosts` is the TV-style picker for the fleet inventory at
`~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`. It mirrors the
[`ssh-config` cable](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/television/cable/ssh-config.toml)
(`tv ssh-config`) but reads fleet's TOML instead of `~/.ssh/config`, so hosts
with explicit `hostname` / `user` / `port` / `identity_file` (no ssh_alias)
are reachable too.

Sister tools: [`fleet exec`](fleet-exec.md) for cross-host ad-hoc commands,
[`fleet pueue`](pueue.md) for queue probing,
[`fleet chezmoi apply`](../this_repo/fleet-apply.md) for the deploy workflow.
All four read the same inventory via `scripts/fleet/apply.py:load_hosts()`.

## Install

Deployed automatically by chezmoi:

- `~/.dotfiles/bin/fleet` — the umbrella binary (dispatches `fleet hosts`)
- `~/.config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` — the TV channel
- `~/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/fleet/hosts.py` — the implementation
  (resolved at runtime via `chezmoi source-path`, so the cable / binary find
  the latest version even on hosts where you haven't run `chezmoi apply` yet)

No separate install step. `tv` (television) is pulled in by the devtools role
and is what powers the picker UX.

## Three entry points

| Form | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `tv fleet-hosts` | Open the picker directly via television. Enter → SSH. |
| `fleet hosts` | Same picker via the fleet umbrella (execs `tv fleet-hosts`). |
| `fleet hosts NAME` | Skip the picker — SSH straight into `NAME`. |
| `fleet hosts --list` | Plain host names, one per line. Scriptable. |
| `fleet hosts --list-tsv` | `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` (the cable's source). |
| `fleet hosts --list-json` | Full inventory as JSON (plain passwords redacted). |
| `fleet hosts --describe N` | Multi-section preview block for `N` (the cable's preview). |
| `fleet hosts --probe N` | BatchMode SSH probe of `N` (the cable's Alt+T action). |

Direct invocation (`fleet hosts NAME`) uses `os.execvp("ssh", ...)`, so your
terminal becomes the SSH session — no wrapper subprocess, no lost TTY
attributes. Behaviour matches Enter inside the picker.

`local = true` hosts are hidden from `--list-tsv` (you can't SSH into
yourself). They still appear in `--list` / `--list-json` for scripts that
want the full inventory. `--include-local` overrides for `--list-tsv` too.

## Keybindings (inside the picker)

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Enter` | SSH into the selected host (`fleet hosts NAME`) |
| `Alt+T` | BatchMode SSH probe — does passwordless login actually work? |
| `Alt+S` | `fleet chezmoi status --hosts NAME` (readiness probe for one host) |
| `Alt+I` | `fleet info --hosts NAME` (OS / CPU / memory / disk snapshot) |
| `Alt+P` | `fleet pueue --hosts NAME` (queue summary for one host) |
| `Ctrl+/` | Toggle preview panel (TV builtin) |

The `Alt+` namespace is used (rather than `Ctrl+letter`) to avoid collisions
with tmux's root-table bindings — see
[CLAUDE.md keybinding rule](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/CLAUDE.md).

## Preview pane contents

`fleet hosts --describe NAME` (which the cable shells out to for every
cursor move) prints four sections:

\```
# host: lab-box        (defined in: /Users/dwlee/.config/fleet/machines.toml)

connection:
  ssh_alias       lab-box
  user            (from ssh_config)
  hostname        (from ssh_config)
  port            (from ssh_config)
  identity_file   (from ssh_config)

fleet metadata:
  local                false
  no_root_machine      false
  chezmoi_path         auto
  password_source      bitwarden (item=ssh-lab-box-sudo)
  extra_env            (none)

ssh -G 'lab-box' (resolved by ssh_config):
  hostname 192.0.2.42
  user dwlee
  port 22
  identityfile /Users/dwlee/.ssh/id_ed25519
  proxyjump bastion.example.com

local key check (offline):
  [OK]   /Users/dwlee/.ssh/id_ed25519
\```

- The `ssh -G` block is omitted for hosts that don't use an `ssh_alias` —
  for those, the explicit fields in the `connection:` section already are
  the resolved values.
- **`password_source` deliberately redacts `type = "plain"` values**. The
  TOML file itself is 0600, but the preview output scrolls into logs /
  screenshots; the type label suffices for triage.

## Subset selection from the picker

TV is single-select. For multi-host fan-out, drop back to the underlying
fleet commands with explicit `--hosts`:

\```bash
fleet hosts --list                # see what's available
fleet exec --hosts self,ts_nas -- pueue --version
fleet info --hosts production_a,production_b
\```

`Ctrl+E`/multi-select pickers are out of scope here — see the
[plan file](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.claude/plans/scripts-fleet-fleet-hazy-boole.md)
for the future-work list.

## Exit codes

| Mode | Exit code |
|------|-----------|
| `--list*` / `--describe` / picker (no SSH happened) | `0` |
| `fleet hosts NAME` (passes to `ssh`) | whatever `ssh` returned |
| `fleet hosts NAME` on a `local = true` host | `0` (no-op) |
| `fleet hosts NAME` on an unknown host | `2` |
| `--probe NAME` | `0` = passwordless OK; `255` = unreachable / auth fail; other = remote command failed |
| Picker fallback when `tv` missing, user aborts | `0` if empty input, `130` on Ctrl-C, `2` on bad index |

## Troubleshooting

- **`tv fleet-hosts` shows no rows**: run `fleet hosts --list-tsv` directly.
  If output is empty, every host has `local = true` (picker hides them).
  Override with `fleet hosts --list-tsv --include-local`.
- **`fleet hosts NAME` prompts for password**: fleet always uses
  non-interactive SSH (key / agent auth). A password prompt means `ssh
  <name>` would also prompt. Fix with `ssh-copy-id`, agent forwarding, or
  the 1Password SSH agent — same fix as
  [`fleet chezmoi apply` unreachable hosts](../this_repo/fleet-apply.md).
- **Preview pane shows `(ssh -G unavailable or returned nothing)`**: the
  alias isn't in `~/.ssh/config` (or its includes). Either add it, or
  switch the host entry to explicit `hostname`/`user`/`port` fields.
- **Alt+S/I/P hangs**: the underlying `fleet chezmoi status` /
  `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` is making one SSH connection — usually
  fast, but a slow remote will block the picker. Press Enter at the
  `[Press Enter to exit]` prompt to return.

## Cross-file invariants

Adding new actions, flags, or output schemas requires touching:

1. `scripts/fleet/hosts.py` — primary implementation
2. `dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet` — USAGE block + `_dispatch_hosts`
3. `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` — picker bindings + preview
4. `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md` — subcommand row
5. `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md` — this page

`_ssh_argv()` in `hosts.py` mirrors the precedence of `_connect_kwargs()` in
`apply.py` (ssh_alias wins over explicit fields). If you change one,
update the other.

The `password_source_arg` redaction rule for `type = "plain"` lives in two
places: `_cmd_describe()` (preview text) and `_cmd_list_json()` (JSON
dump). Both must stay in sync.

97	The umbrella discovers the chezmoi source dir at runtime via `chezmoi

106	
107	### Note on `fleet chezmoi status` overload
108	
109	`fleet chezmoi status` has two modes. Default (`fleet chezmoi status` /
110	`--quick`) is the **pre-flight readiness probe** — read-only, ~1.5s/host,
111	predicts what `fleet chezmoi apply` would do. Adding `--live` flips it to

1	"""fleet exec — cross-host ad-hoc command runner.
2	
3	Fan-out an argv-list command (or shell string) over the fleet inventory:
4	
5	  1. Default: argv list after `--`, no shell expansion (safe by construction).
6	     `fleet exec -- pueue --version` runs `pueue --version` literally on each
7	     host via asyncssh; per-arg shlex.quote keeps it injection-safe.
8	  2. `--shell <bin>` opt-in: wraps in `<bin> -c '<argv joined>'` so the user
9	     can use pipes / globs / redirects / env-prefixes.
10	  3. `--login` opt-in: wraps in `<shell> -lc '...'` so the remote rc files
11	     load (gives access to nvm / mise / conda / aliases). Slower per host.
12	  4. `--ai` summarises results into succeeded/differed/failed tiers via the

16	Per-host failures (SSH timeout, command exit ≠ 0) never abort the run; each
17	shows up as its own row with rc + first line of stderr.
18	
19	Output: Rich table by default; `--json` for piping; `--out-dir DIR` writes
20	per-host stdout/stderr/json files; `--full-output` expands the table into
